findings.claim: The maxStepUp doc comment says applying it on every track is 'fine while no replay baselines exist (before G3)'. Replay baselines now exist and G3 enforces them, so the comment is stale. It also suggests a global physics change is still acceptable, which is a trap: CLAUDE.md requires new physics to be opt-in per track, car or surface.
findings.evidence: src/sim/car.ts:76-79: "/** Highest step a grounded car can climb in one tick; ... (see MAX_RAMP_SLOPE). It applies on every track: fine while no replay baselines exist (before G3). */ maxStepUp: 0.3," — the baselines are present: tests/baselines/replay-states.json and tests/baselines/replays/{drift,jump,prop-collision,car-contact,bot-race}.json. PHASE0_STATUS.md:140 lists 'G3 physics replays' as an active gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the last sentence with one saying the value is part of the recorded replay behaviour (G3 baselines), so it must not change; a different step rule has to be opt-in per track, car or surface. Comment only.

findings.claim: Two sim comments describe the game as it was earlier. TrackData.width says the width is '8.4 per UI_RULES §9', but registered tracks use 11. The bot.ts header calls the bot 'the race opponent' and 'its line', but player races now run five bots (one per roster AI driver).
findings.evidence: src/sim/types.ts:15: "/** Track ribbon width in units (8.4 per UI_RULES §9). */" vs src/content/tracks/dust-bowl.json:5 "width": 11 (bends.json:5 is 8.4; in-flight hay-loop is 11). src/sim/bot.ts:1: "// Bot driver: the race opponent, and the driver the bot-lap gate (G2) uses on every track." vs merged #20 (B04): six-car races, 'each driven by its own seeded bot'.
findings.suggestedFix: types.ts:15: change to 'Track ribbon width in units (e.g. 8.4, the UI_RULES §9 reference).' bot.ts:1: change to 'Bot driver: drives every AI car in a race, and the car the bot-lap gate (G2) uses on every track.' Comments only.

findings.claim: validateTrack copies every prop row twice. The map at line 224 already builds a fresh object literal per row, then line 240 spreads each one into another new object. The second copy does nothing.
findings.evidence: src/sim/track.ts:224: "return { kind: k, side, from, to, spacing, offset } as const;" and src/sim/track.ts:240: "propRows: propRows.map((r) => ({ ...r }))," — ramps (line 197/239) and props (line 230/241) are returned directly without a second copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the 'as const' at line 224 (side is already narrowed to 'left' | 'right' by the check at line 217) and return 'propRows' directly at line 240, matching ramps and props. Same values, one allocation fewer per row.

findings.claim: The positive-modulo wrap ((v % n) + n) % n is written out by hand five times in track.ts: for spline control points, arc length and three segment indices. A small helper in vec.ts would give identical results.
findings.evidence: src/sim/track.ts:286 "points[((i % n) + n) % n]"; :429 "((s % t.length) + t.length) % t.length"; :461 "((segment % track.count) + track.count) % track.count"; :497 "((hintSeg % n) + n) % n"; :504 "(((centre + o) % n) + n) % n".
findings.suggestedFix: Add 'export function wrapIndex(v: number, n: number): number { return ((v % n) + n) % n; }' (named for what it does) to src/sim/vec.ts and use it at the five sites. It runs the exact same operations, so results stay bit-identical.
